# `Q-5-58` — Social Image Needs `site-url`

> A page's Open Graph or Twitter Card preview image was left out because `website.site-url` is not set, and social media sites need an absolute image URL.

## What this means

A website with `open-graph` or `twitter-card` enabled writes
`og:image` and `twitter:image` tags so that a shared link shows a
preview image. Social media sites fetch that image on their own, from
outside your site, so the tag must hold an absolute URL such as
`https://example.com/images/cover.png`.

Quarto builds that URL from `website.site-url`. This site doesn't set
one, so Quarto can't, and it leaves the image tags out rather than
writing a relative path no crawler can follow. The other tags (title,
description, card type) are still written.

## Why this happens

The site enables social metadata:

```yaml
website:
  title: My Site
  open-graph: true
```

and the page has a preview image: an `image:` in its front matter, an
image in its body, or a site-wide `website.image`.

## How to fix

Set `site-url` to the address the site is published at:

```yaml
website:
  title: My Site
  site-url: https://example.com
  open-graph: true
```

If you don't want preview images, set `image: false` on the page to
stop Quarto looking for one in its body.
